ideas.title: Simplicity certificate: Res_{F_{2^n}/F_2}E has no non-product sub-abelian varieties or Prym quotients over F_2 at prime n with 2 primitive
ideas.statement: For prime n with ord_n(2)=n-1, the F_2-Frobenius phi on R=Res_{F_{2^n}/F_2}E has char poly P_E(T^n) (E/F_{2^n}) resp. (T^2-tT+2)*Psi(T) (E defined over F_2, Psi of degree 2(n-1)). Claim: P_E(T^n) (random E) and Psi (Koblitz) are irreducible over Q, so R (resp. the trace-zero part A) is F_2-simple; every F_2-sub-abelian variety, Prym-type quotient or isogeny factor is 0, R/A or isogenous to the whole thing. Closes the 'non-product sub-abelian variety over F_2' branch of the lens.
ideas.mechanism: Irreducibility of the Weil polynomial over Q implies simplicity (Tate). For Koblitz, Psi roots are zeta*tau, zeta in mu_n\{1}; [Q(sqrt-7,zeta_n):Q]=2(n-1) and zeta*tau generates it.
ideas.wall_bypassed: None (theory item); it sharpens 'No subfield, no low-degree membership' from the Frobenius-subspace statement to the abelian-variety statement and bounds LEAD-ICB-ecc2k130-jacobian-carrier from below (any carrier Jacobian over F_2 has genus >= n-1 and contains A as a factor).
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The subspace closure is about F_2-linear subspaces of F_{2^n}; sub-abelian varieties of R are a different object (could be non-linear in coordinates). This item checks whether that extra room exists. Expected: it does not.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: None; obstruction/theory. If irreducibility FAILS for some E, a proper F_2-sub-abelian variety A' of dim < n-1 would be a genuine smaller-dimensional descent target (Gaudry/Diem IC on A'(F_2) via a curve in A'), the only way this lens could push B*D^2 below N.
ideas.prior_art: Tate 1966 (isogeny classes via Weil polynomials); Galbraith-Smart Weil descent; Gaudry-Hess-Smart 2002; Menezes-Qu 2001 (GHS fails for prime n); Diem 2003 (GHS for odd characteristic / prime degree analysis); Lange trace-zero varieties.
ideas.novelty_status: novelty_unverified (expected known folklore; value is as a filed closure certificate)

ideas.title: Prym-factor carrier over F_2: Jacobians of genus g in (n-1, 2(n-1)] having the trace-zero A as an isogeny FACTOR rather than isogenous to it
ideas.statement: Generalise LEAD-ICB-ecc2k130-jacobian-carrier from 'A ~ Jac(C)' to 'Jac(C) ~ A x B' with C/F_2 of genus g between dim A and 2 dim A (Prym-type). IC in Jac(C)(F_2) at large genus over tiny field is L_{2^g}(1/2); at g~200 roughly 2^53 GAE-equivalents vs rho 2^64.9 (heuristic, setup excluded). Question: is the frequency of curves with A as a factor at genus g larger than the Torelli codimension heuristic for g = dim A, enough to change the 2^-(codim) rarity?
ideas.mechanism: Divisibility of L_C(T) by the fixed Weil polynomial Psi of A. Isogeny factor = shared L-factor (Tate). The DLP moves via the F_2-rational map A -> Jac(C) (dual of Jac(C)->A), which is a homomorphism, so Transport conservation applies but only to kernel size, not to the destination-arithmetic gain, which is the whole point.
ideas.wall_bypassed: Torelli-rarity heuristic (8,128) underlying the closure of the Jacobian-carrier lead, and the 'Transport conservation' wall (which explicitly leaves destination arithmetic free).
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The rarity heuristic counts Jacobians ISOGENOUS to A (dim moduli 3g-3 vs dim A_g = g(g+1)/2 at g=dim A). For g>dim A the condition is only that A is a factor; the count of such curves is not governed by that codimension, and Prym loci (double covers) are a natural source.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: If such C of genus g<=~2 dim A were constructible, Jac(C)(F_2) IC is a field-representation (divisor-smoothness) algorithm, not generic; its L(1/2) cost at g=260 is below rho in the heuristic model. Getting the curve is the obstruction; this idea only measures whether the factor condition is easier than isogeny.
ideas.prior_art: LEAD-ICB-ecc2k130-jacobian-carrier; Gaudry-Hess-Smart; Menezes-Qu; Diem 'index calculus in class groups of non-hyperelliptic curves'; Enge-Gaudry L(1/2) for large genus over small fields; Kani-Rosen decompositions; Prym constructions (Mumford). ECDLP-IDEA-002 uses split Jacobians over F_p (different: E is the factor at same field).

ideas.title: Miller cocycle telescopes to an elliptic-net ratio: U(kP) = c * W(k)/W(k-1) up to N-th roots, so LEAD-TRF-miller-cocycle reduces to Lauter-Stange EDS problems
ideas.statement: With gcd(N,p-1)=1, U(R)=f_{N,P}(R)^{1/N}. Translation: div(f(.+P)/f) = N div(1/(x-x_P)), so U(R+P)/U(R) = c/(x(R)-x_P) and x(jP)-x_P = -psi_{j-1}psi_{j+1}/psi_j^2 (P). Product over j<k telescopes: U(kP) = C * (W(k)/W(k-1)) * W(1)-normalisation, W the elliptic net at P. Hence U is a function of the point that equals an elliptic-divisibility-sequence ratio; its log carries k-structure iff the EDS residue/association problems are easier than ECDLP, which Lauter-Stange 2008 shows they are not (EDS association equivalent to ECDLP; residue problem reduces to F_p^* DLP only through the Tate pairing, trivial here).
ideas.mechanism: Explicit identity linking the unexamined Miller-cocycle transfer to elliptic nets (closed as GGM-simulable for computing, KN-FIND), plus a character test of any residual quadratic-exponential structure W(k) -> alpha^{k^2} beta^k W(k).
ideas.wall_bypassed: Transport conservation (homomorphic only) - U is non-homomorphic, the listed gap.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: Transport-conservation lemma needs a homomorphism; U is not one. The identity shows the gap is filled by the EDS literature + GGM-simulability of elliptic nets, not by Transport conservation.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Would be non-generic only if chi_l(U(kP)) or log U(kP) mod small l | p-1 depended on k by a low-degree law; the quasi-period factor of W is the Tate pairing value which is 1 here, so prediction is no structure: closure, accounting class.
ideas.prior_art: Lauter-Stange 2008 (EDS and ECDLP equivalences); Stange 2007 elliptic nets and Tate pairing; Shipsey thesis 2000; Miller 2004; LEAD-TRF-miller-cocycle-nonhom-transfer; ECDLP-IDEA-007/164.
ideas.novelty_status: novelty_unverified (identity is standard; its use to close the lead is the contribution)

ideas.title: CEILIDH/torus factor bases collapse to inverted-affine subspace bases: x = u+1/u with u in T_2 parametrised rationally gives 1/x affine-F_2-linear in the parameter
ideas.statement: Norm-one torus T_2(F_{2^n}) in F_{2^{2n}}, rational CEILIDH parametrisation u=(a+theta)/(a+theta^q), a in F_{2^n}. Then x=u+1/u = (theta+theta^q)^2/(a^2+s a+N_theta), s=Tr theta, and a -> a^2+s a is F_2-linear. So the torus base {x(u): a in V} for an F_2-subspace V equals {x : c/x in L(V)+N_theta} = an affine subspace in the 1/x coordinate (2-to-1). Every 'torus-based factor base' (XTR/CEILIDH style, including Dickson/mu_M images u+1/u) with subspace-parametrised u is a Mobius-relabelled subspace base. Prediction: same descended solving degree as a plain subspace base in the y=1/x Semaev presentation.
ideas.mechanism: Additivity of the Artin-Schreier-type map a^2+sa in characteristic 2 linearises the torus parametrisation after inversion.
ideas.wall_bypassed: Claims to bypass 'No subfield, no low-degree membership' (torus sets are non-subspace in x); this idea shows it does not.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: They do not fail: the torus base is a subspace in 1/x, so Weil descent proceeds exactly as for a subspace base; the residual difference is the presentation (S_3 in 1/x is S_3 transformed by x->1/x, same multidegree 2).
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Constant factor at best (presentation change of the measured d_F). Classified relabelling; closes torus-parametrised bases with subspace-parameter for lever 6. Only u ranging over non-subspace parameter sets (e.g. mu_M with M | 2^n+1) escapes, and that is the corpus mu_263 / multiplicative-subgroup item.
ideas.prior_art: Rubin-Silverberg CEILIDH 2003; Lenstra-Verheul XTR 2000; Granger-Vercauteren torus index calculus 2005; Diem/Gaudry subspace descent; Petit-Quisquater; LEAD-ICB-nonlinear-frob-stable-bases (mu_263).

ideas.title: Upward embedding E(F_p) -> E(F_{p^n}) with trace back-projection: base-size accounting shows B >= p for every F_p-linear base, so the descent analogue cannot go below N
ideas.statement: Decompose R in E(F_p) inside E(F_{p^n}) over a base F_V = {P in E(F_{p^n}) : x(P) in V}, V an F_p-subspace, then apply Tr: E(F_{p^n}) -> E(F_p) to get nR = sum Tr(P_i). The effective base is Tr(F_V) in E(F_p). Integer dim V >= 1 forces |F_V| ~ p^{dim V} >= p ~ r unless V restricted to non-subspace sets, which brings back the prime-field membership wall. Also: for V = c F_p, Tr(P) for P with x in cF_p are points of E(F_p) whose distribution is uniform, so the effective base has size ~min(p,|F_V|).
ideas.mechanism: Weil restriction of the summation polynomial over F_{p^n}/F_p with target in the subfield; trace as back-transfer (homomorphism, Transport conservation applies to it).
ideas.wall_bypassed: Attempted: 'No subfield' for prime p by manufacturing a subfield upstairs.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: They hold: the subfield created upstairs is F_p itself, the base must have size p^{integer}; B*D^2 >= p ~ N. Records the obstruction precisely for the lens 'embedding E(F_p) into E(F_{p^n})'.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: None; accounting. B >= p means B*D^2 >= N regardless of D.
ideas.prior_art: Gaudry 2009, Diem 2011 (E(F_{p^n}) descent); Semaev 2004; Petit-Kosters-Messeng 2016 (PKM towers, prime field); treatise extension.tex / prog_prime.tex.
